tomato_early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
tomato_early_blight.description: Dark brown circular lesions with distinct concentric target-board rings on tomato leaflets. Lower leaves turn chlorotic yellow and drop prematurely.
tomato_early_blight.treatment: Chemical: Apply Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Chlorothalonil (2 g/L) or Hexaconazole 5% SC (1 ml/L). Organic: Spray cold-pressed Neem oil (5 ml/L) or Trichoderma harzianum.
tomato_early_blight.prevention: Stake plants and prune bottom foliage to improve airflow and keep leaves away from soil-borne spores.

tomato_late_blight.name: Tomato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)
tomato_late_blight.description: Aggressive, dark water-soaked necrotic lesions rapidly expanding across tomato foliage, petiole, and green fruit, with white downy fungal growth on underside in humid air.
tomato_late_blight.treatment: Chemical: Spray Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Cymoxanil (2 g/L) or Dimethomorph (1 g/L) immediately. Organic: Preventive Copper Hydroxide (2.5 g/L).
tomato_late_blight.prevention: Plant blight-resistant tomato cultivars. Ensure strict spacing (>60 cm) and eliminate volunteer potato/tomato culls.

tomato_bacterial_spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot (Xanthomonas spp.)
tomato_bacterial_spot.description: Small, water-soaked, dark brown to black angular lesions surrounded by distinct bright yellow chlorotic halos. As spots coalesce, leaf margins turn brown and ragged.
tomato_bacterial_spot.treatment: Chemical: Apply Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L) tank-mixed with Streptomycin Sulphate / Kasugamycin (0.5 g/L). Organic: Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis (5 g/L).
tomato_bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds. Avoid working in fields when plants are wet to prevent mechanical spread.

tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.name: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot (Septoria lycopersici)
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.description: Numerous small, circular spots (2-3 mm) with dark brown margins and light gray or tan centers containing minute black pycnidia. Causes rapid bottom-up defoliation.
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Chemical: Apply Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) or Difenoconazole (0.5 ml/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L). Organic: Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L) or bio-fungicide Trichoderma viride.
tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch soil around plants. Remove infected lower leaves immediately upon symptom onset.

tomato_yellow_leaf_curl.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV)
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl.description: Leaves exhibit severe upward and inward curling, prominent interveinal chlorosis (yellowing), and leaf size reduction. Plants become stunted. Transmitted by Whitefly.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl.treatment: No chemical cure for viral infections once established. Vector Control: Apply Thiamethoxam 25% WG (0.3 g/L) or Acetamiprid 20% SP (0.4 g/L). Roguing: Uproot infected plants.
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl.prevention: Install 40-50 mesh insect-proof nets in nurseries. Deploy yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre). Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrid varieties.

tomato_leaf_mold.name: Tomato Leaf Mold (Passalora fulva)
tomato_leaf_mold.description: Pale yellow chlorotic patches on the upper leaf surface accompanied by velvety olive-green to purple-gray fungal sporulation on the corresponding lower surface.
tomato_leaf_mold.treatment: Chemical: Apply Chlorothalonil (2 g/L) or Trifloxystrobin + Tebuconazole (0.7 g/L). Organic: Potassium Bicarbonate (4 g/L) or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
tomato_leaf_mold.prevention: Maintain greenhouse relative humidity below 80% with ventilation fans. Space plants for maximum airflow.

tomato_spider_mites.name: Tomato Two-Spotted Spider Mite (Tetranychus urticae)
tomato_spider_mites.description: Fine yellow-white stippling (pinpoint speckling) across the upper leaf surface, progressing to bronzing and leaf desiccation. Fine silky webbing visible on leaf undersides.
tomato_spider_mites.treatment: Chemical: Spray Acaricides — Abamectin 1.9% EC (0.5 ml/L) or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (1 ml/L) or Fenazaquin 10% EC (1.5 ml/L). Organic: Apply Neem oil (5 ml/L).
tomato_spider_mites.prevention: Keep field borders weed-free. Maintain adequate soil moisture to reduce dry stress conditions preferred by spider mites.

tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus (ToMV / TMV)
tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Mottled pattern of alternating dark green and light green/yellow patches on foliage, accompanied by blistering, puckering, and leaf distortion.
tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: Direct Treatment: No chemical cure. Immediately isolate and destroy symptomatic foliage. Disinfect pruners and tools with 10% TSP or bleach.
tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Disallow tobacco use near crop fields. Use certified virus-free seedling stocks. Wash hands before touching plants.

tomato_target_spot.name: Tomato Target Spot (Corynespora cassiicola)
tomato_target_spot.description: Small pinpoint brown lesions that expand to circular spots with tan centers and dark brown margins. Distinct concentric rings form in mature spots.
tomato_target_spot.treatment: Chemical: Apply Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) or Boscalid (1 g/L) or Chlorothalonil (2 g/L). Organic: Copper Hydroxide (2.5 g/L).
tomato_target_spot.prevention: Improve row spacing to increase canopy airflow. Rotate out of solanaceous crops.

tomato_healthy.name: Tomato — Healthy Foliage
tomato_healthy.description: Tomato foliage exhibits uniform vibrant chlorophyll pigmentation, intact serrated composite leaflets, and healthy venation with no spotting or chlorosis.
tomato_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Continue standard balanced N-P-K fertigation.
tomato_healthy.prevention: Maintain regular weekly crop scouting and biosecurity protocols.

potato_early_blight.name: Potato Early Blight (Alternaria solani)
potato_early_blight.description: Dark brown to black circular lesions with distinct concentric target-board rings on potato foliage, surrounded by a narrow chlorotic halo. Starts on older bottom leaves.
potato_early_blight.treatment: Chemical: Apply Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Chlorothalonil (2 g/L) or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (1 ml/L). Organic: Spray Copper Hydroxide (2.5 g/L) or Neem oil.
potato_early_blight.prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops. Use drip irrigation to prevent spore splash.

potato_late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)
potato_late_blight.description: Rapidly expanding water-soaked, dark olive-brown to black necrotic lesions on leaves and stems. Under cool humid conditions, white downy mildew sporulates on leaf underside.
potato_late_blight.treatment: Chemical: Spray immediately with Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold @ 2.5 g/L) or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (2 g/L) or Dimethomorph (1 g/L). Destroy heavily infected plants.
potato_late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers. Avoid overhead irrigation during cool humid periods.

potato_healthy.name: Potato — Healthy Foliage
potato_healthy.description: Potato compound foliage exhibits vibrant green pigmentation, smooth ovate leaflet margins, and healthy vascular structure.
potato_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain scheduled irrigation and potassium hilling.
potato_healthy.prevention: Scout lower canopy weekly for early blight onset during canopy closure.

corn_common_rust.name: Corn Common Rust (Puccinia sorghi)
corn_common_rust.description: Small, powdery, oval to elongate cinnamon-brown to golden-orange pustules (uredinia) scattered across both upper and lower surfaces of corn leaf blades.
corn_common_rust.treatment: Chemical: Spray Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole (Amistar Top @ 1 ml/L) or Pyraclostrobin (1 ml/L) or Propiconazole 25% EC (1 ml/L). Organic: Apply Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L).
corn_common_rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrid maize varieties. Practice early planting to avoid peak airborne urediniospore dispersal periods.

corn_gray_leaf_spot.name: Corn Gray Leaf Spot (Cercospora zeae-maydis)
corn_gray_leaf_spot.description: Distinctly rectangular, narrow tan to gray necrotic lesions bounded strictly by parallel leaf veins. Lesions coalesce under humid conditions, causing severe foliar blighting.
corn_gray_leaf_spot.treatment: Chemical: Apply Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad (Priaxor @ 0.6 ml/L) or Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) at tasseling stage (VT/R1). Organic: Foliar bio-fungicide Trichoderma harzianum.
corn_gray_leaf_spot.prevention: Implement minimum 2-year crop rotation with non-host crops (soybeans). Manage corn residue through tillage in high-risk zones.

corn_northern_leaf_blight.name: Corn Northern Leaf Blight (Exserohilum turcicum)
corn_northern_leaf_blight.description: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) developing on lower leaves and progressing upwards across the canopy.
corn_northern_leaf_blight.treatment: Chemical: Apply Propiconazole 25% EC (1 ml/L) or Azoxystrobin + Cyproconazole (1 ml/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L). Organic: Spray Bacillus subtilis foliar bio-fungicide.
corn_northern_leaf_blight.prevention: Select maize hybrids carrying Ht resistance genes. Practice crop rotation and bury infected residue after harvest.

corn_healthy.name: Corn / Maize — Healthy Foliage
corn_healthy.description: Elongated Gramineae leaf blades exhibit uniform green chlorophyll pigmentation, clear parallel venation, and intact structural margins.
corn_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain balanced nitrogen-potassium top dressing.
corn_healthy.prevention: Scout weekly for fall armyworm and foliar rust during vegetative stages.

apple_scab.name: Apple Scab (Venturia inaequalis)
apple_scab.description: Olive-green to dark brown circular or irregular velvety lesions developing on leaves and fruit. As lesions mature, leaves become distorted, puckered, and defoliate prematurely.
apple_scab.treatment: Chemical: Apply Captan 50 WP (2.5 g/L) or Myclobutanil 10% WP (0.5 g/L) or Difenoconazole 25% EC (0.5 ml/L). Organic: Spray Wettable Sulphur (3 g/L) or Potassium Bicarbonate (4 g/L).
apple_scab.prevention: Prune canopy to promote air circulation. Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eradicate overwintering pseudothecia.

apple_black_rot.name: Apple Black Rot (Botryosphaeria obtusa)
apple_black_rot.description: Small purple specks on upper leaf surface that enlarge into circular 'frog-eye' leaf spots with light brown centers and distinct dark purple margins.
apple_black_rot.treatment: Chemical: Spray Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Thiophanate-methyl (1 g/L) or Copper Hydroxide (2.5 g/L). Organic: Apply Copper Oxychloride early in season; prune all dead wood.
apple_black_rot.prevention: Prune out dead shoots and cankered branches at least 15 cm below visible infection. Destroy mummified fruit on trees and orchard floor.

apple_cedar_rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust (Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae)
apple_cedar_rust.description: Bright yellow-orange to reddish-orange circular spots on upper leaf surface. Small black pycnidia form in the center, followed by tube-like aecia on lower surface.
apple_cedar_rust.treatment: Chemical: Apply Myclobutanil (0.5 ml/L) or Trifloxystrobin (0.5 g/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L). Organic: Spray Sulfur formulations before infection periods.
apple_cedar_rust.prevention: Remove nearby Eastern Red Cedar / Juniper trees within a 1-mile radius where possible. Plant resistant apple cultivars.

apple_healthy.name: Apple — Healthy Foliage
apple_healthy.description: Apple foliage exhibits uniform chlorophyll pigmentation, intact leaf blade margins, and healthy venation with no symptoms of scab or foliar rust.
apple_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain scheduled orchard nutrition and irrigation.
apple_healthy.prevention: Implement standard preventive scouting and bio-stimulant foliar applications.

grape_black_rot.name: Grape Black Rot (Guignardia bidwellii)
grape_black_rot.description: Small, circular reddish-brown necrotic spots with dark borders on upper leaf surface, containing minute black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) arranged in a ring.
grape_black_rot.treatment: Chemical: Apply Myclobutanil (0.5 ml/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Kresoxim-methyl (0.5 g/L) from bud break through veraison. Organic: Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L).
grape_black_rot.prevention: Prune and destroy infected canes and mummified berry clusters. Train vineyard canopy for optimal sunlight and aeration.

grape_esca.name: Grape Esca / Black Measles (Phaeomoniella chlamydospora)
grape_esca.description: Characteristic 'tiger-stripe' interveinal chlorosis and necrosis, where yellow-red bands bordered by green veins dry out and turn brown, causing premature leaf drop.
grape_esca.treatment: No direct chemical cure for established systemic wood infections. Protect pruning wounds immediately with pruning sealant containing Thiophanate-methyl or Trichoderma.
grape_esca.prevention: Disinfect pruning shears between vines with 70% alcohol. Avoid pruning during wet weather.

grape_leaf_blight.name: Grape Leaf Blight (Pseudocercospora cladosporioides)
grape_leaf_blight.description: Dark brown to black angular necrotic spots on leaves with reddish-purple halos. Lesions dry out, causing leaves to curl and drop prematurely.
grape_leaf_blight.treatment: Chemical: Apply Copper Oxychloride (3 g/L) or Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L). Organic: Foliar neem oil (5 ml/L) or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
grape_leaf_blight.prevention: Ensure adequate trellis spacing and summer leaf thinning to reduce humidity around the grape canopy.

grape_healthy.name: Grape — Healthy Foliage
grape_healthy.description: Palmate grape foliage displays rich, uniform green chlorophyll coloration, intact palmate lobes, and clear venation with no necrotic spotting.
grape_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Continue standard vineyard micronutrient program.
grape_healthy.prevention: Maintain regular weekly canopy scouting and prophylactic sulfur dusting.

pepper_bacterial_spot.name: Pepper Bacterial Spot (Xanthomonas campestris)
pepper_bacterial_spot.description: Small, water-soaked, dark brown to black circular or angular lesions surrounded by distinct bright yellow chlorotic halos on bell pepper and chili foliage.
pepper_bacterial_spot.treatment: Chemical: Apply Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L) tank-mixed with Streptomycin Sulphate (0.5 g/L) at early symptom onset. Organic: Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis (5 g/L).
pepper_bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds. Avoid overhead irrigation to prevent bacterial dissemination.

pepper_healthy.name: Bell Pepper — Healthy Foliage
pepper_healthy.description: Glossy, vibrant green bell pepper foliage with smooth intact margins and clear acute apex.
pepper_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain scheduled watering and calcium-magnesium fertigation.

wheat_stripe_rust.name: Wheat Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis)
wheat_stripe_rust.description: Distinct linear stripes or rows of bright yellow-orange powdery pustules developing parallel to leaf veins on wheat blades. Causes premature leaf desiccation.
wheat_stripe_rust.treatment: Chemical: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (1 ml/L) or Tebuconazole 250 EC (1 ml/L) or Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) at first appearance of stripe pustules. Organic: Copper Hydroxide.
wheat_stripe_rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant wheat varieties. Eliminate volunteer wheat and grass weeds in field margins.

wheat_leaf_rust.name: Wheat Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina)
wheat_leaf_rust.description: Scattered circular to oval reddish-orange powdery pustules (uredinia) on the upper surface of wheat leaves.
wheat_leaf_rust.treatment: Chemical: Apply Propiconazole 25% EC (1 ml/L) or Pyraclostrobin (1 ml/L). Organic: Spray sulfur bio-formulation.
wheat_leaf_rust.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars. Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer.

wheat_powdery_mildew.name: Wheat Powdery Mildew (Blumeria graminis)
wheat_powdery_mildew.description: White fluffy powdery fungal patches on lower wheat leaves and stems, turning dull gray-brown with black cleistothecia as crop matures.
wheat_powdery_mildew.treatment: Chemical: Spray Epoxiconazole (1 ml/L) or Metconazole (1 ml/L) or Hexaconazole (1 ml/L). Organic: Potassium Bicarbonate (4 g/L).
wheat_powdery_mildew.prevention: Avoid dense crop seeding rates. Select resistant seed stock.

wheat_healthy.name: Wheat — Healthy Foliage
wheat_healthy.description: Slender linear wheat leaves show uniform green color, intact margins, and no rust pustules or powdery fungal patches.
wheat_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain balanced N-P-K nutrition.
wheat_healthy.prevention: Monitor field during tillering and stem elongation stages.

rice_leaf_blast.name: Rice Leaf Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae)
rice_leaf_blast.description: Spindle-shaped / diamond-shaped lesions with grayish-white centers and dark brown or reddish-brown borders. Lesions coalesce rapidly, killing entire leaves.
rice_leaf_blast.treatment: Chemical: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP (0.6 g/L) or Isoprothiolane 40% EC (1.5 ml/L) or Kasugamycin 3% SL (1.5 ml/L). Organic: Spray Neem oil with bio-control agents.
rice_leaf_blast.prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization. Maintain continuous field flooding during critical vegetative stages.

rice_brown_spot.name: Rice Brown Spot (Bipolaris oryzae)
rice_brown_spot.description: Oval to circular, sesame-seed-shaped dark brown lesions with gray or whitish centers and yellowish halos distributed across elongated rice leaves.
rice_brown_spot.treatment: Chemical: Apply Tricyclazole 75% WP (0.6 g/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Carbendazim (1 g/L). Organic: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (5 g/L).
rice_brown_spot.prevention: Treat seeds with hot water (52-54°C) or bio-fungicides. Ensure balanced soil potassium and silicon nutrition.

rice_bacterial_blight.name: Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae)
rice_bacterial_blight.description: Water-soaked to yellowish-green wavy stripes on leaf margins starting at leaf tips, turning straw-yellow and drying out into white-gray scorched blades.
rice_bacterial_blight.treatment: Chemical: Spray Streptomycin + Tetracycline (0.5 g/L) and Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L). Organic: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens (5 g/L).
rice_bacterial_blight.prevention: Drain flooded field temporarily. Avoid clipping rice seedling tips during transplanting.

rice_healthy.name: Rice — Healthy Foliage
rice_healthy.description: Erect, vibrant green paddy leaves with clean parallel veins and no blast or brown spot lesions.
rice_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain scheduled water regime and silicon fertilization.
rice_healthy.prevention: Scout nursery and tillering stages weekly.

cotton_bacterial_blight.name: Cotton Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum)
cotton_bacterial_blight.description: Angular, water-soaked brown to black lesions bounded by small leaf veins on palmately lobed cotton leaves, often spreading down the main leaf vein (blackarm).
cotton_bacterial_blight.treatment: Chemical: Apply Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L) + Streptocycline (0.1 g/L). Organic: Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis.
cotton_bacterial_blight.prevention: Delint and treat acid-delinted cotton seeds. Destroy infected crop stalks post-harvest.

cotton_leaf_curl.name: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuD)
cotton_leaf_curl.description: Upward or downward leaf curling, pronounced vein thickening (enation) on leaf undersides, and extreme stunting of plants. Transmitted by Whitefly.
cotton_leaf_curl.treatment: No chemical cure for virus. Manage whitefly vector with Pyriproxyfen 10% EC (1 ml/L) or Diafenthiuron 50% WP (1 g/L).
cotton_leaf_curl.prevention: Eradicate alternate weed hosts (Abutilon indicum). Plant CLCuD-tolerant cotton hybrids.

cotton_healthy.name: Cotton — Healthy Foliage
cotton_healthy.description: Broad palmately lobed cotton foliage exhibits deep green color, smooth surface, and strong vascular integrity.
cotton_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain scheduled irrigation and potash spray.
cotton_healthy.prevention: Deploy pheromone and sticky traps early in the season.

soybean_rust.name: Soybean Asian Rust (Phakopsora pachyrhizi)
soybean_rust.description: Tiny tan to dark brown volcanic-shaped pustules (uredinia) on the underside of trifoliate leaves with yellow chlorotic speckling on upper surfaces.
soybean_rust.treatment: Chemical: Apply Azoxystrobin + Cyproconazole (0.6 ml/L) or Trifloxystrobin + Prothioconazole (0.7 ml/L) immediately at first detection. Organic: Copper Hydroxide.
soybean_rust.prevention: Monitor early vegetative canopy. Plant early-maturing soybean varieties.

soybean_sudden_death.name: Soybean Sudden Death Syndrome (Fusarium virguliforme)
soybean_sudden_death.description: Interveinal chlorotic spots coalesce into bright yellow patches that turn necrotic brown between veins, leaving only main veins green.
soybean_sudden_death.treatment: Fungicide seed treatment with Fluopyram (ILeVO). No effective foliar rescue once foliar symptoms appear.
soybean_sudden_death.prevention: Improve field drainage to reduce soil compaction. Rotate with non-host crops.

soybean_healthy.name: Soybean — Healthy Foliage
soybean_healthy.description: Trifoliate soybean leaves show uniform deep green coloration, intact ovate leaflets, and vigorous growth.
soybean_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain balanced soil phosphorus and Rhizobium nodulation.
soybean_healthy.prevention: Scout field weekly from R1 flowering stage onward.

citrus_canker.name: Citrus Canker (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri)
citrus_canker.description: Raised, corky, blister-like brown lesions on leaves and twigs surrounded by a characteristic distinct oily, water-soaked chlorotic yellow halo.
citrus_canker.treatment: Chemical: Apply Copper Hydroxide (2.5 g/L) + Streptocycline (0.1 g/L) during flush flushes. Organic: Bordeaux mixture (1%).
citrus_canker.prevention: Install windbreaks around orchards. Prune and burn infected shoots during dormancy.

citrus_black_spot.name: Citrus Black Spot (Phyllosticta citricarpa)
citrus_black_spot.description: Small round sunken reddish-brown spots on leaves and fruit peel with gray centers and elevated black margins.
citrus_black_spot.treatment: Chemical: Apply Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Pyraclostrobin (0.5 ml/L) or Copper Oxychloride (3 g/L). Organic: Horticultural oil spray.
citrus_black_spot.prevention: Remove fallen leaf litter under tree canopy before rain season.

citrus_greening.name: Citrus Greening / Huanglongbing (Candidatus Liberibacter)
citrus_greening.description: Asymmetrical blotchy foliar mottle crossing leaf veins, yellow shoots ('yellow dragon'), and small bitter lopsided fruit. Transmitted by Citrus Psyllid.
citrus_greening.treatment: No cure for infected trees. Aggressive vector control: Imidacloprid (0.5 ml/L) or Thiamethoxam. Uproot infected trees in early-stage orchards.
citrus_greening.prevention: Plant certified disease-free nursery stock under screenhouse. Deploy psyllid monitoring traps.

citrus_healthy.name: Citrus — Healthy Foliage
citrus_healthy.description: Glossy, dark green citrus leaves with smooth winged petioles, strong aroma, and clear vascular structure.
citrus_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain scheduled micronutrient foliar spray (Zn, Mn, Fe).

cucumber_powdery_mildew.name: Cucurbit Powdery Mildew (Podosphaera xanthii)
cucumber_powdery_mildew.description: Talcum powder-like white fungal colonies expanding over upper and lower leaf surfaces, leading to yellowing, browning, and premature leaf crisping.
cucumber_powdery_mildew.treatment: Chemical: Apply Trifloxystrobin (0.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) or Myclobutanil (0.5 ml/L). Organic: Spray Potassium Bicarbonate (4 g/L) or Neem oil (5 ml/L).
cucumber_powdery_mildew.prevention: Select powdery mildew-tolerant hybrid cucumber varieties. Space plants to allow full sun exposure.

cucumber_downy_mildew.name: Cucurbit Downy Mildew (Pseudoperonospora cubensis)
cucumber_downy_mildew.description: Angular, bright yellow chlorotic patches strictly delimited by leaf veins on the upper surface, with purplish-gray downy mold on the underside.
cucumber_downy_mildew.treatment: Chemical: Spray Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (2 g/L) or Fluopicolide (1 ml/L) or Metalaxyl (2 g/L) immediately. Organic: Copper Hydroxide (2.5 g/L).
cucumber_downy_mildew.prevention: Avoid overhead watering. Maintain excellent greenhouse ventilation.

cucumber_anthracnose.name: Cucurbit Anthracnose (Colletotrichum orbiculare)
cucumber_anthracnose.description: Circular yellowish or water-soaked spots that enlarge, turn dark brown, and dry out, leaving 'shot-hole' perforations in the leaf blade.
cucumber_anthracnose.treatment: Chemical: Apply Chlorothalonil (2 g/L) or Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L). Organic: Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L).
cucumber_anthracnose.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds. Rotate with non-cucurbit crops for 2-3 years.

cucumber_healthy.name: Cucumber / Cucurbit — Healthy Foliage
cucumber_healthy.description: Broad triangular-lobed green leaves with hairy margins, healthy venation, and intact lamina.
cucumber_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain drip fertigation.
cucumber_healthy.prevention: Scout lower canopy weekly for downy or powdery mildew.

strawberry_leaf_scorch.name: Strawberry Leaf Scorch (Diplocarpon earlianum)
strawberry_leaf_scorch.description: Numerous small, dark purple or reddish-purple spots on upper leaf surfaces that enlarge and coalesce, giving foliage a burned or scorched appearance.
strawberry_leaf_scorch.treatment: Chemical: Spray Captan 50 WP (2.5 g/L) or Thiophanate-methyl (1 g/L) or Difenoconazole (0.5 ml/L). Organic: Copper Hydroxide (2 g/L).
strawberry_leaf_scorch.prevention: Remove dead foliage in early spring. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

strawberry_healthy.name: Strawberry — Healthy Foliage
strawberry_healthy.description: Trifoliate strawberry leaves exhibit rich emerald green pigmentation, serrated margins, and vibrant healthy stolons.
strawberry_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain balanced calcium and potassium feeding.
strawberry_healthy.prevention: Ensure proper raised bed straw mulching.

coffee_leaf_rust.name: Coffee Leaf Rust (Hemileia vastatrix)
coffee_leaf_rust.description: Yellowish oily spots on upper leaf surface corresponding to powdery, bright orange-yellow fungal pustules on the lower leaf surface, causing severe defoliation.
coffee_leaf_rust.treatment: Chemical: Apply Copper Oxychloride (3 g/L) or Cyproconazole (1 ml/L) or Pyraclostrobin (0.8 ml/L). Organic: Preventative Bordeaux mixture (1%).
coffee_leaf_rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant coffee cultivars (Catimor / Castillo). Manage shade tree canopy to 30-40% cover.

coffee_healthy.name: Coffee — Healthy Foliage
coffee_healthy.description: Glossy, dark green, elliptical coffee leaves with prominent undulating margins and clean central vein.
coffee_healthy.treatment: No pathological treatment required. Maintain scheduled shade regulation and organic compost.
coffee_healthy.prevention: Monitor leaves during onset of rainy season.
